entries.def: when you experience an intense and overpowering feeling of delight.
when you are satisfied with what you have.
entries.example: You can say 'She is content' or 'She is contented' but only 'a contented person'.

entries.def: when life is looking bright and positive.
when someone has done something thoughtful for you.
when something has happened that gives you great pleasure, when you hear news of someone's good fortune, for instance.
when everything seems wrong in your life.
when your life is not giving you satisfaction.
when you have had enough of something disagreeable.
entries.example: You could be fed-up with someone's rudeness, or sick (and tired) of someone's behaviour.

entries.def: when you are miserable over a long period of time.
entries.example: Depression is considered an illness in some severe cases.

entries.def: when you are unable to do something that you want to do.
when you cannot make sense of different conflicting feelings or ideas; mixed up is more colloquial.
when you are expecting something special to happen, e.g. before a party.
when you are stimulated to create deeds or words.
entries.example: You might feel inspired by a really talented musician to learn how to play a musical instrument.

entries.def: when you have very positive feelings about something, enthusiastic about, e.g. a new project.
when something extremely exciting and pleasing happens.
entries.example: She was thrilled when the film star kissed her.

entries.def: when you are angry or bad-tempered.
entries.example: It is often, though not exclusively, used about small children. Stop getting so cross with me.

entries.def: when you are extremely angry; livid and seething are more informal; in a rage/fury also mean furious or violently angry.
when you are afraid and uncertain about the future.
entries.example: I am so anxious about the results of my exams that I can't sleep.

entries.def: when you are afraid or anxious about something that is about to or may be about to happen.
entries.example: I feel nervous about going to the dentist. Feeling nervous is a little bit like feeling excited but it is a negative feeling whereas excitement is positive.

entries.word: apprehensive about, e.g. an important meeting
entries.def: when you are slightly nervous or anxious about something in the future.
when anxious thoughts constantly go through your head.
when something unpleasant has happened to disturb you.
entries.example: It often combines feelings of both sadness and anger.

note: Left page only; presentation is a 'You feel: word + when-clause' list under two headings. Right page is exercises and was not extracted. Pos markers, IPA and sense numbers are not printed.
